editorial:
Get ready for another round of undercover disguise comedy as FBI agent Malcolm Turner teams up with his teenage son Trent for a wild adventure at an all-girls performing arts school. After Trent witnesses a murder, the two go undercover as Big Momma and her niece Charmaine to track down the killer before he tracks them down. The vibe is loud, colorful, and packed with slapstick moments that lean hard into fish-out-of-water humor. You get dance numbers, awkward situations, and plenty of moments where the disguises almost slip. It is not trying to be deep or serious, and that is part of its charm. If you enjoyed the earlier Big Momma movies, you will feel right at home here.

The acting is energetic, especially from Martin Lawrence, who throws himself into the physical comedy with full commitment. The action scenes are light and fun rather than intense, and the pacing keeps things moving without dragging too much. On the downside, some jokes feel recycled and the story is pretty predictable, so do not expect big surprises. Still, it is a decent pick for a relaxed movie night with friends or family. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want to own it.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Malcolm and Trent finally corner the murderer at the school after a chaotic chase through the campus. The killer is exposed during a big performance, and the crowd watches as the truth comes out. Malcolm drops the Big Momma disguise to reveal himself, while Trent steps out of the Charmaine costume. With the bad guy caught and the evidence secured, father and son share a moment of bonding. They leave the school behind, their undercover mission complete, and head home with a stronger relationship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slapstick undercover comedies and lighthearted family movie nights.
